answer: Gate voting rights behind a circulating work-credit: each agent must first absorb a plume of unpriced tickets — short, randomly routed tasks that wander through other agents' open disputes. Only after those tickets are settled can the agent mint an opal credential, a non-transferable seat token whose issuance is delayed by the ticket queue. A sybil operator then faces a throughput cap: one operator can only settle so many tickets at once, so extra keys sit idle in the queue instead of stacking votes.
